peri-megadim/1:_: By Ner 20 17 and Beer the Ghola Daya A. Karev and Daya B. Kashmuel and EBI and they are B. excuses in the Rash Ya'Sh. And AMSH comes with the letter B. E. of this:
peri-megadim/2:_: Unless — Taz in Tosafot note 27, see there; 27, see there. Shabbat 23b — and Taz questioned there: if he does not intend his weights there is bizuy mitzvah for nothing; not so here, for he will kindle a second time. And "from candle to candle" implies it is permitted even to kindle a Chanukah candle in his hand from a candle attached to the wall — and although it is permitted to do so even when kindling is the mitzvah, if he holds it for some time and then attaches it afterward it is permitted, as in siman 675 letter 3 according to his view there; and therefore from the mere statement "from candle to candle" it implies even in such a case it is permitted. And why should we not be concerned that while he pulls it out and places it in its place the candle will go out and he will have kindled the first kindling for nothing — nevertheless it is permitted. And Olot Reiyah letter 2: nevertheless the first kindling combines for the half-hour measure, see there — meaning that once he has kindled, the kindling is a mitzvah and there is no bizuy, and we do not concern ourselves with denial at all; and even though we establish that he must leave it in its place afterward, nevertheless there is no bizuy as above — and if so Tosafot write well. And Olot Reiyah adds another explanation of "from candle to candle": one moves a candle that is placed and already burning to a candle attached to the wall and kindles with it, see there. And at the end, in seven methods he explained that which we say: if kindling is the mitzvah — one kindles from candle to candle; if placing is the mitzvah — one does not kindle, for kindling is required before placing — and therefore it is impossible with long wicks; and if kindling is the mitzvah one kindles with long wicks, see there. This implies that when kindling is the mitzvah one must attach the wick first and kindle afterward — unlike Taz below in siman 675:3, for otherwise it could occur without long wicks with both in his hand. And the expression "from candle to candle" — he did not say "candle from candle" — one can explain: from a mitzvah candle to another that will become a mitzvah candle; for both are certainly in his hand and both are still non-sacred; when placing is the mitzvah one kindles. And per what Tosafot said — moving a burning Chanukah candle to an attached candle to kindle — one need not use long wicks; and in siman 672 it implies one may not move a burning Chanukah candle while it burns, see there end.
